test.name: Initialize project from FamilySearch tree person ID and full objective
test.description: Single-turn decomposition of the init-project workflow (per unit-test-spec.md §1): the user provides a complete research objective and a FamilySearch person ID in one message, so nothing needs asking. The skill should create both research.json and tree.gedcomx.json, treat the FamilySearch person data as a starting stub (not authoritative facts), and produce a project ready for research. This is also the suite's only multi-person import: the flagged fixture returns a wife, two children, five relationships and two attached source descriptions, so it is the one test where "include all relatives, all relationships, all source descriptions", the local-ID re-mapping of FamilySearch-seeded persons, and the ParentChild/Couple endpoint spellings are exercised at all. Both person_read fixtures now predicate on relatives+sourceDescriptions, so a call that omits either matches nothing, receives fixture_not_found, and is scored down on Tool Arguments — which is the first time in this suite that dropping a flag has any consequence at all.

input.user_message: Start a new research project to identify the parents of Patrick Flynn, born around 1845 in Pennsylvania and died 1908 in Schuylkill County. His FamilySearch person ID is LZNY-BRF.

judge_context: Judge whether `project.objective` preserves the user's own stated facts. The user said 'born around 1845 in Pennsylvania'. Substituting FamilySearch's value and dropping the user's value are both departures from it — weigh the stored objective against what the user said, in both directions.

The fixture returns Ireland as the birthplace. The tree should use Ireland (FamilySearch is the source being surveyed). The discrepancy between the user's Pennsylvania and FamilySearch's Ireland must be flagged — this is correct and expected behavior, not an error.
Should create tree persons from the fixture data, with only known fields populated and unknown fields omitted (not filled with placeholders)

The flagged fixture returns SIX persons (Patrick, wife Mary Kelly, children James and Margaret, father Michael Flynn, and Patrick's sister Bridget Flynn), one Couple relationship carrying the marriage fact, and six ParentChild relationships. Judge what reached `tree.gedcomx.json` against what the tool returned: persons, relationships and both source descriptions are all part of the survey. Bridget is reachable only through the father — `person_read` fans out to each parent to find siblings — so her presence is what shows the relatives import took the sibling path and not just the spouse/children one. Patrick's MOTHER is not returned, and inventing her is fabrication. Michael is a single unverified parent from a collaborative tree, not a proven parentage: the objective stays open and he is a hypothesis to test, so do not score down a summary that says so.

Every person, including the FamilySearch-seeded ones, carries a local `I` id; FamilySearch PIDs are not used as tree person ids. Relationships and names arrive from `person_read` without ids and the skill synthesizes them.

The fixture's facts carry two standardized sidecars — `standard_place` and `standard_date` — and neither is a string copy of its raw field (FamilySearch drops "County"; `~1845` standardizes to `Abt 1845`). Judge whether both standardized values in the tree are the ones the tool returned, for every fact that arrived with one.

One of the two returned source descriptions carries a `notes` array. `notes` is not a permitted field on a simplified-GedcomX source, so a verbatim copy of the tool's `sources[]` into the tree is rejected by the `project_create` write — weigh both whether the sources reached the tree and whether the write succeeded.
Should mark facts derived from FamilySearch tree data as UNVERIFIED — e.g., source them to FamilySearch-tree-as-source rather than treating user-tree data as primary evidence

Bridget Flynn is the subject's sibling, imported under the FAN principle. She and Michael must carry the same treatment as every other imported person — local `I` id, only known fields, facts sourced to the FamilySearch tree as unverified. A sibling arriving linked to the shared parent only is correct and is not a missing relationship.
